Baklava: Thin pastry leaves with ground nuts and honey.
Okroshka: Cold soup of diced meats, scallions, eggs, cucumbers, sour cream and kvass.
Eggplant Orientale: Cold chopped eggplant baked with tomatoes and onions.
Beef a La Stroganoff: Lean beef with fresh mushrooms in sour cream sauce.
Pelmeny Siberian: Chopped beef and veal dumplings, served in consomme with fresh dill and mustard sauce and sour cream on the side.
Eggplant a la Russe: Eggplant baked in sour cream sauce, en casserole au gratin.
Bitochki: Chopped chicken and veal patties, Stroganoff sauce.
Golubtze: Stuffed cabbage with tomatoes, onions, sauerkraut and sour cream sauce.
Pirojok: Meat-filled pastry served with soups.
Blinchiki: Thin crepes filled with cottage cheese, apple or cherry preserves, with sour cream and powdered sugar.
Green Schi: Spinach soup with onions and fresh dill, served with hard boiled egg, hot or cold.
Roszolnick: Chicken giblet soup with pickles and a variety of vegetables.
Blini: Thin buckwheat pancakes with caviar, sour cream and hot melted butter.
Kasha a la Gourieff: Hot sweetened farina with fruit and apricot sauce and toasted almonds.
Russian Cream: Whipped cream and ice cream garnished with grenadine and sliced almonds.
Borscht (Cold): Chilled soup of beets and cucumbers served with sour cream and fresh dill.
Kissel: Puree of cranberries served with cream.
Salade Olivier: Chicken salad with potatoes, onions, eggs, apples and pickles.
Kulebiaka: Chicken, salmon or cabbage loaf, baked in pastry shell with rice, eggs and mushrooms, cream sauce.
Borscht (Hot): Soup of beets, cabbage and tomatoes served with sour cream and fresh dill.
Shashlik Caucasian: Marinated leg of spring lamb, broiled on skewer with tomatoes, green pepper and onions.
Lodchka (Little Boat): Chocolate-covered mocha-filled macarooon pastry.
Chakhobili: Spring chicken stewed with tomatoes and onions en casserole.
Karsky Shashlik: Marinated saddle of spring lamb, broiled and served with rice and red cabbage.
Luli Kebab: Chopped sirloin of lamb patties, broiled, mushroom sauce.
Chicken Tabaka: Whole squab chicken pressed and sauteed, served with tart prune sauce.
Schi: Soup of brased sauerkraut, root vegetables and tomatoes, served with sour cream.
Mushrooms a la Russe: Fresh mushrooms baked in sour cream sauce en casserole, au gratin.
Charlottka: Charlotte Russe.
Sirniki: Baked sweetened cottage cheese patties, powdered sugar, sour cream.
Cotelettes Boyar: Chopped veal and chicken patties with mushroom sauce.
Mussaka: Oriental casserole dish made of spring lamb, eggplant, cheese and tomatoes, baked in layers.
Meat Solyanka: Soup made with diced meat, dill pickles, onions and capers, served with sour cream and olives.
Cotelette a la Kiev: Boned breast of chicken stuffed with butter, breaded and baked.
Nalistniki: Crepes stuffed with pate, mushroom sauce.
Cotelette de Volaille: Breast of chicken, stuffed with chopped chicken and baked, crouton crust.
Strawberries Romanoff: Fresh strawberries with Cointreau and whipped cream.
Noisette of Spring Lamb: Marinated lamb steak, sauteed.
Ogurtze Salad: Sliced cucumbers, radishes, scallions, sour cream and yougurt dressing, fresh dill.
Chopped beef and veal or salmon patties, special sauce.
Zakuska: Hors d'Oeuvres a la Russe.

Yang Chow Chow Fon: Fried rice, in the Yang Chow manner, with Chinese mushrooms, eggs, bits of roast pork, etc

Li-Chee: these are preserved fresh li-chee from China; a heavenly desert. (Most people erroneously think of li-chee as "nuts", because of the raisin-like dried fruit)

Traditional English Afternoon Tea- Served approx. 1 1/2 hours prior to landing
Afternoon Tea- A Great British Tradition- Tea, the most universally consumed of all drinks, is especially popular in Britain where the annual consumption is something in the region of 512 million cups. W. E. Gladstone observed "If you are cold, tea will warm you- if you are heated, it will cool you- if you are depressed, it will cheer you- if you are excited, it will calm you." First brought to England c. 1559 by Giambattista Rusmusio, tea did not evolve into an afternoon meal until the end of the 18th century. Anna, Duchess of Bedford, invented afternoon tea to fill the long gap between early lunch and dinner which bored many house parties. It became a meal surrounded by etiquette and customs, delicate china, silver, cake stands and doilies- a time when friend and family meet. Famous tea parties include Mad Hatter's (Alice's Adventures in Wonderland by Lewis Carroll 1865), the Boston Tea Party, 1773, and not forgetting HM Queen Elizabeth II's annual garden parties at Buckingham Palace. The Duke of Wellington declared that "Tea cleared my head and left no misapprehensions." He was right- tea contains small amounts of two B vitamins, and has no calories, artificial flavourings or colourings. It is said to cure gout, apoplexy, epilepsy, gall stones and sleepiness, and one's longevity is assured.  "Thank God for Tea! What would the world do without tea?"- Sydney Smith
